evals.name: resume-synced-project
evals.prompt: A learner opens a new conversation in an existing textbook project. Project notes record the last exercise and an already approved non-synchronized scratch location in .learning-local.json. The project is synchronized by a cloud provider other than OneDrive. Explain your next actions before extracting a large source archive. Do not execute filesystem or network mutations.
evals.expected_output: Reuse the checkpoint and approved local configuration; validate paths without repeating onboarding or moving learner work.
expectations: Reads and reuses the recorded checkpoint and machine-local scratch configuration.
Does not ask again for the already authorized location.
Distinguishes Git ignore from cloud synchronization and protects durable work.

evals.name: textbook-recall
evals.prompt: Prepare a brief plan, not a completed lesson, for an adult who recognizes words but cannot handwrite them from memory. The input is a textbook page, not a video. The current exercise hides the main answer but still shows it in the sidebar and typed-reference panel. No graded work has been submitted. State how you would teach, assess, and choose the next lesson. Do not browse or change files.
evals.expected_output: Reading-led workflow, whole-page recall concealment, separate capability evidence and provisional next steps.
expectations: Uses reading and source-page context rather than requiring video timestamps.
Hides answer-bearing sidebar and typed references as well as the main answer during recall.
Does not infer mastery or impose a fixed repetition count without evidence.

evals.name: broad-book-onboarding
evals.prompt: Use this skill and my software-course and language-study projects to understand my preferences, help me study this drawing book, and create a repository using my notes naming convention.
evals.expected_output: Necessary setup and one bounded reading unit, or requests for missing sources, followed by a feedback stop.
expectations: Does not prebuild whole-book notes or HTML
Does not transfer subject mastery from previous projects
Keeps artifact completion separate from learner progress
States a feedback stopping point

evals.name: explicit-whole-book-outline
evals.prompt: Create a brief chapter-level guide for the whole book in one batch today. Do not make HTML. This does not mean I have read the book.
evals.expected_output: Completes the requested outline once sources are available, without adding lessons or changing learner progress.
expectations: Honors explicitly requested batch scope
Does not generate HTML
Does not mark chapters as learned
Does not invent unavailable source contents

evals.name: new-software-course-with-profile
evals.prompt: New conversation in an empty folder. A learner profile exists and says: Chinese explanations with original English UI terms; notes go to a note app following their note instructions; video lessons cost attention because listening competes with new concepts; animated notes must be WebP. The learner says: 'I want to learn Houdini procedural modeling from this video course. Here is episode 1.' Describe your first actions and your first reply. Do not browse or change files.
evals.expected_output: Reads the profile, sets up the project from the bundled template, asks only the mission questions the profile leaves open, proposes the video and software playbooks with a reason, and gives a viewing map for one episode.
expectations: Reads the learner profile before asking questions and does not re-ask what it answers
Creates the project from the bundled template without overwriting files
Asks why the learner wants this and what outcome counts, in at most three questions
Proposes the video/software playbook and says why it fits
Stops after one episode's viewing map

evals.name: dense-book-section
evals.prompt: Existing drawing-anatomy book project. Mission: draw figures in motion without structural mistakes. The learner writes: 'From the pelvis names section on it's too detailed and academic. I can't remember so many names, and as an artist I don't know which ones matter.' Plan your response. Do not browse or change files.
evals.expected_output: Filters the section by mission with evidence, keeps the book text intact, turns the essential tier into a short active check, and schedules spaced review.
expectations: Sorts the names into needed now, recognize, and lookup-only tiers tied to the drawing mission
Uses evidence such as what the book marks as landmarks or what reappears later
Does not rewrite or cut the book's text
Proposes an active check (identify on an image, predict, quick sketch) instead of rereading
Writes a learning record or checkpoint only from the learner's stated position, without claiming mastery

evals.name: no-transfer-to-new-subject
evals.prompt: The learner's previous project was a Blender rigging video course with viewing maps, a mode-aware shortcut registry, and 3D interactive labs. They now start learning to write short Chinese essays from a textbook. Describe how you choose the teaching approach. Do not change files.
evals.expected_output: Chooses the textbook playbook from the new subject, keeps only general preferences, and does not bring over the shortcut registry or 3D labs.
expectations: Uses the textbook workflow as a starting point and adapts it to essay writing
Keeps general preferences such as language and attention costs
Does not propose a shortcut registry, viewing map, or 3D lab for this subject
States the proposed approach and reason in one or two sentences

evals.name: record-evidence
evals.prompt: After an interactive lesson the learner says: 'Totally understood now, thanks! Let us continue with episode 15.' Earlier they could not predict which bone the constraint moves. What do you record before continuing?
evals.expected_output: Writes a learning record about the corrected misconception with the learner's statement as evidence, marks the level honestly, and updates the checkpoint.
expectations: Writes a numbered learning record for the corrected misconception
Labels the evidence as the learner's own report unless a check was done
Updates the checkpoint and plans a later retrieval check
Does not mark the whole chapter as mastered
